events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected.

* WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 202 PM MST, a streamflow gauge near Dateland continues to
steadily rise and is now showing a depth of just above 7.5 feet
with flow around 1250 cfs. This gauge is forecasted to reach
action stage (8 ft) on Friday. Flooding is expected along the
Gila River within the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, 1 1/2 to 2 1/2 ft of
inundation above ground level expected in vulnerable areas near
the waterfront and shoreline. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, 1
to 1 1/2 ft of inundation above ground level possible in
vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline.

* WHERE...Northeast Suffolk County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Thursday to 6
AM EST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 8 AM to 4
PM EST Friday.

* COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread moderate flooding of
vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline, including
roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes and businesses
with basements near the waterfront. Numerous road closures are
likely, and vehicles parked in vulnerable areas near the
waterfront will likely become flooded. Flooding will also
extend inland from the waterfront along tidal rivers and bays.

* SHORELINE IMPACTS...Breaking waves of 4 to 8 ft will result in
areas of dune erosion and localized overwashes. Wave splashover
will exacerbate flooding of roadways and vulnerable structures
behind protective dunes and seawalls. There is potential for
isolated damage to shoreline and marina structures as well.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest water levels are likely with
the Thursday morning and evening high tides. The forecast has
been leaned towards a higher end water level scenario to provide
a bit of safety margin. If the timing of strongest winds is
quicker than currently forecast the peak water level forecast
could be increased by a few tenths for Thursday morning. if
slower the Thursday morning forecast could be lowered slightly.
Similarly if strongest winds linger later into the evening, the
Thursday evening water level forecast could be a few tenths
higher.

events.summary:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, 2 to 3, locally 3 1/2 ft,
of inundation above ground level expected in vulnerable areas
near the waterfront and shoreline. For the Coastal Flood Watch,
up to 1 1/2 to 2 1/2 ft of inundation above ground level
possible in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline.

* WHERE...Southwest Suffolk County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Thursday to 6
AM EST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Friday
morning through Friday afternoon.

* COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread moderate to locally major
flooding of vulnerable areas near the waterfront and
shoreline, including roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and
homes and businesses with basements near the waterfront.
Numerous road closures are likely, and vehicles parked in
vulnerable areas near the waterfront will likely become
flooded. Flooding will also extend inland from the waterfront
along tidal rivers and bays.

* SHORELINE IMPACTS...Breaking waves of 8 to 12 ft will result
in widespread beach flooding and dune erosion during times of
high tide. There is potential for localized overwashes
resulting in some flooding of roadways and vulnerable
structures behind protective dunes.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest water levels are likely with
the Thursday morning and evening high tides, potentially
extending into the Friday morning high tides. The forecast has
been leaned towards a higher end water level scenario to
provide a bit of safety margin. If the timing of strongest
winds is quicker than currently forecast the peak water level
forecast could be increased by a few tenths for Thursday
morning. if slower the Thursday morning forecast could be
lowered slightly.
